draft.title: Kinship, moieties and totems
card: Kinship
a system that sets out how each person is related to others, and what they owe to them. It covers family, but also reaches beyond it to the wider community.
Moiety
one of two main groups that a community is divided into. Each person belongs to one moiety, and it shapes their relationships and roles.
Totem
a plant, animal or natural feature that a person or group has a special connection to. It carries responsibilities to look after that species and its place on Country.
Together these set out each person's relationships, roles and responsibilities to other people and to Country. They are passed on through lore, which is taught from generation to generation.
draft.remember: Kinship, moieties and totems tell each person who they are connected to and what they must care for.

a.q: What do kinship systems, moieties and totems do for a First Nations community?
opts: Set out each person's roles and responsibilities
Decide which families may live on which island
Record the dates of important events in the past
Show how far each group may travel for food
a.why: These systems set out how people relate to each other and to Country, and what they are responsible for. They are not maps or calendars, so the options about travel and dates are wrong.

b.q: A young girl is taught that her totem is a particular bird, and that she has a duty to care for it and the place where it lives. What does this show about totems?
opts: They link a person to Country with responsibilities
They are a game played between two groups
They are a name given only to the oldest person
They are a tool used for hunting that bird
b.why: A totem is a connection to a species or feature, and it brings responsibilities to look after it and its place on Country. It is not a tool or a game, and the card does not limit it to the oldest person.
b.clue: Look at what the girl must do for the bird.

b.best: They link a person to Country with responsibilities

The moiety definition reads as if every First Nations community is split into two moieties. Moiety systems are common but not universal, and many nations use section or subsection systems instead. The card should say many communities are divided this way.
Why (a) explains only why the travel and dates options are wrong. It does not deal with the island option, so the explanation is incomplete.
